messages:
emily: Quick question - noticed 'Effective quota' in console for api-service is 30r/s but router reports 50r/s for route /v1/chat. Not sure how they diverged, filing here before I dig deeper.
frank: Huh, can you paste the config snippets you applied? Might be an override layering thing.
emily: pasted minimal config we rolled today:
```
defaults:
  quota: 30
routes:
  - path: /v1/chat
    quota: 50
    owners: [team-chat]
```
Console shows 30 on the service summary, route view shows 50.
greg: That's expected if console summary uses the "service-level effective" calc (defaults + policy) and route view shows route-level override. But they should align when you inspect route in detail. Are we sure the UI isn't mixing cached vs live?
emily: I refreshed and still mismatch. Also noticed metric dim: `requests_quota_limit{service=\"api-service\"}` is 30, while `router_quota_config{route=\"/v1/chat\"}` is 50.
frank: So three different sources: (1) config store effective policy, (2) router-applied config, (3) console cached interpretation. We need single source of truth. Which component is authoritative for billing/ratelimiting? Router should be authoritative at runtime.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: config apply cfg-2026-05 to staging at 1769501107 :rocket:
greg: Proposal: annotate metrics emitted by router with `config_origin=\"router\"` and `config_hash=<short>` and export `config_applied{route,...}`. Then change console to prefer router-backed metric for quota display when available, falling back to config-store derived value.
emily: That sounds good. Short-term debug: add a small hover/help text in console explaining that service summary may be an aggregate default and route overrides exist. Avoid users thinking quota is silently lower.
frank: Also we should add an internal API: GET /config/effective?scope=route&route=/v1/chat that returns merge stack so UI can show how final value was computed. It should include timestamps and source (console, infra, preview).
greg: Implementation note: config-store currently flattens overrides on read, but doesn't expose provenance. We can add lightweight `provenance` field with list of applied layers. Minimal change: record last applied `config_hash` and `applied_at` on the router when it ack's an apply.
emily: Ops ask: any risk if console flips to router metric? Could be lag during rollout. We need fallback to avoid spikes in displayed values.
frank: Yes, do a feature flag for 2-week rollout: console.prefers_router_quota=true. Toggle off if dashboards/alerts regress.
ops-bot: monitoring-bot: created alert rule candidate: if |router_quota - console_quota| / console_quota > 0.2 for >5m -> page oncall.
emily: I'll open three tickets: infra/metrics -> router labels + config_hash; platform/api -> effective-config API; console -> UI copy + feature flag. Assigning to @frank for API, @greg for exporter + metrics, @emily for console copy.
greg: I'll prototype exporter change today and wire a test metric `config_trace{route=\"/v1/chat\",config_hash=\"abc123\",origin=\"router\"}`.
frank: I'll spec the GET /config/effective endpoint and include examples of returned merge stack.
emily: Great. Once we have config_hash in metrics we can also power a new dashboard that shows drift between config-store and router-applied settings.
frank: Nice. That will help ops confidence during large rollout windows.
emily: Thanks team. I'll link the tickets here when created. :white_check_mark:
